And Another on 24 July, 2025 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD Neutral Citation No. - 2025:AHC:122404 Reserved on : 03.07.2025 Delivered on : 24.07.2025 Court No. - 79 Applicant :- Vishal Kumar Tiwari Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Alok Kumar Mishra,Savan Kumar Counsel for Opposite Party :- Abhinav Shukla,G.A.,Ram Shiromani Shukla Hon'ble Prashant Kumar,J. 1. Heard Shri Sushil Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State opposite party no.1 and perused the record. 2. The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed for quashing the impugned order dated 18.01.2024 passed by Additional Sessions Judge /F.T.C. Court No. 1, Prayagraj, in Sessions Trial No. 659 of 2023 (State vs. Ram Kailash and others), under Section 376, 452, 323, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Handia, District Prayagraj, by which the application of the applicant filed under section 227 Cr.P.C. on 09.01.2024 was rejected. Vishal Kumar Tiwari vs State Of U.P. And Another on 24 July, 2025 1 3. Facts enumerated in the instant application is that the informant-prosecutrix is Chachi (Aunty) of the applicant. She and her husband had long existing property dispute with the father and other uncles of the Applicant, which was filed by her husband namely Ramfer Tiwari before the Civil Judge (S.D.), Prayagraj registered as Original Civil Suit No. 1280 of 2019 and the same is pending. 4. As per the allegation contained in the F.I.R. which was lodged by the informant-prosecutrix, one Ram Kailash Tiwari who is father of the Applicant had committed rape upon her on several occasions on 18.3.2019, 1.5.20219 and 29.6.2019 by threatening her on gun point and when she disclosed these facts to the villagers, on 02.07.2019 the said accused Ram Kailash Tiwari along with his two sons namely Applicant and Shubham as well as his two nephew namely Suraj and Amit forcefully entered into the house of prosecutrix and assaulted her. On intervention of villagers, they left her by threatening with dire consequences. 5. After lodging of the F.I.R. against Ram Kailash Tiwari (father of the Applicant), Applicant, his brother and cousins namely Shubham, Suraj and Amit, Investigating Officer proceeded and recorded statement under section 161 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix stated that it was her family dispute and accused Ram Kailash Tiwari was her Jeth who did not do anything to her and that she had reconciled with him and she no longer was interested in prosecution. 6. However, in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C., she reiterated the allegations as levelled in the FIR assigning role of committing rape upon her, only to the Ram Kailash Tiwari, who is father of the applicant. In so far as role of the Applicant and his 3 other brothers and cousin are concerned, she merely alleged about assault committed by them on 2.7.2019. Importantly, she admitted that she and her husband were having family property disputed with Ram Kailash Tiwari and his family. 7. Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of State of Haryana Vs. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 has laid down the guidelines in para 41 and 102, under which circumstances the Court should, in its inherent power, entertain an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. The guidelines are as follows:- " 41. Inherent power given to the High Court under Section 482 CrPC is with the purpose and object of advancement of justice. In case solemn process of Court is sought to be abused by a person with some oblique motive, the Court has to thwart the attempt at the very threshold. The Court cannot permit a prosecution to go on if the case falls in one of the categories as illustratively enumerated by this Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, Judicial process is a solemn proceeding which cannot be allowed to be converted into an instrument of operation or harassment. When there are materials to indicate that a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive, the High Court will not hesitate in exercise of its jurisdiction under Section 482 CrPC to quash the proceeding under Category 7 as enumerated in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal. 102. (7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge." 26. Looking into the facts and circumstances of the case, all the steps can only be answered in the affirmative. This Court, therefore have no hesitation whatsoever in concluding, that on the basis of the material available on record, the rejection of the discharge application (impugned order herein) is not justified, it is fit case where the applicant on the basis of evidence on record ought to have been discharged.
